page: Microsoft Azure E32bds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor on the x86_64 architecture. The server allocates 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The configuration includes 256 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU, alongside a 48 MB L3 cache and hardware support for cryptographic acceleration and AVX-512 instruction sets.

Integrated local storage is provided via a 1288 GB solid-state drive, complementing the instance block storage capabilities. No discrete GPU acceleration is included, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. System execution is managed under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations position the memory subsystem in the upper performance tier, with PassMark memory scoring in the top 25 percent and uncached read bandwidth reaching 151.75 GB/sec. General CPU computation falls within standard median brackets, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 13440 and a PassMark CPU score of 36975.23. High-throughput in-memory evaluations show Redis processing up to 31.6 million set operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 34.04 GB/sec. Large model inference reveals architectural bounds on CPU-only execution, where 70B parameter prompt processing drops into the bottom 25 percent tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance targets memory-dense environments where high RAM capacity and dedicated fast scratch storage offset the need to step up to larger compute nodes. It is suited for in-memory caching layers, relational database servers, medium-scale data analytics, and intermediate ETL staging pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E32bds_v5 is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C architecture running at 2.8 GHz. The instance is configured with 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores, 256 GB of system memory, and a bundled 1288 GB local SSD. It does not include a GPU. Benchmarks show upper-quartile memory performance with a strong PassMark memory rating and uncached read bandwidth of 151.75 GB/sec, while multi-core compute throughput and database operations align with general industry averages. Redis caching throughput reaches 31.6 million operations per second, and text generation on small language models achieves above-average efficiency. The high memory-to-core allocation of 8 GB per vCPU combined with local NVMe-class storage makes the E32bds_v5 cost-effective for memory-constrained workloads, including relational database engines, distributed caching clusters, and ETL data transformation pipelines.
